Apple is actively expanding its South Bay real estate footprint in 2025, and has now grown its Sunnyvale presence once again. Here's what we know.

Apple continues to expand its footprint

According to the Mercury News (via AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease a 125,800-square-foot office building at 580 N. Mary Ave. in Sunnyvale.

The deal marks Apple's first major real estate transaction in the area in 2026, following a spending spree in 2025 that saw the company invest more than $1 billion to expand its South Bay presence.

The expansion included the $166.9 million purchase of a three-building campus known as "Gateway" in Cupertino, the $350 million acquisition of Sunnyvale's two-building Mathilda Commons campus, and a $365 million purchase of the four-building Mathilda Campus next door.

Apple later spent another $216 million on two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its total Bay Area expansion in 2025 to over 1.5 million square feet of office and lab space.

Returning to the new lease, the Mercury News noted that the deal comes as South Bay office leasing activity has started to rebound, with vacancy rates improving from both the prior quarter and the year-ago quarter:

According to a report from Colliers, South Bay office vacancy was 14.1% in Q2 2026. Colliers defines the market as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

The report also noted that, in addition to Apple, Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Ave. in Sunnyvale.
